article.headline: OpenAI Codex Arrives as a Plugin Inside Claude Code
article.lede: A new open-source plugin lets developers run OpenAI's Codex software-engineering agent directly from within Anthropic's Claude Code environment. The integration is built on the same open-source server and harness that underpin Codex itself, meaning users get the full feature set — parallel task execution, model access, and code-review workflows — without leaving their existing IDE toolchain.
article.body:
OpenAI's **Codex** is a cloud-based software-engineering agent launched in May 2025. It is powered by *codex-1*, a version of the o3 reasoning model fine-tuned on real-world coding tasks using reinforcement learning. Each task Codex receives runs in its own isolated cloud sandbox preloaded with the user's repository; the agent can read and edit files, run test harnesses, propose pull requests, and work on multiple tasks simultaneously. Completion time typically falls between one and thirty minutes depending on complexity.

The plugin discussed in the tweet — `openai/codex-plugin-cc` on GitHub — brings that capability into *Claude Code*, Anthropic's command-line coding assistant. The repository's own description is blunt: "Use Codex from Claude Code to review code or delegate tasks." Because the plugin shares the same open-source app server and harness as the standalone Codex product, the feature parity is genuine rather than a stripped-down bridge.

What makes this notable is the cross-company plumbing it represents. Anthropic and OpenAI are direct competitors in the frontier-model market, yet a plugin authored under the `openai` GitHub organisation is designed to slot into Anthropic's tooling. The integration is possible because both Claude Code and the Codex harness expose open interfaces — neither requires proprietary lock-in at the plugin layer.

The poster, @romainhuet, is a developer-relations figure at OpenAI who has frequently promoted Codex since its launch. His framing — "my favorite thing" — signals that the architectural decision to build on open-source components was deliberate, not incidental, and is intended as a selling point for developers evaluating whether to adopt the agent.

concepts.definition: A cloud-based software-engineering agent from OpenAI, launched May 2025. It accepts coding tasks via prompt, executes them in isolated sandboxed environments preloaded with the user's codebase, and can handle many tasks in parallel. It is distinct from the earlier Codex code-completion API.

The model powering OpenAI's Codex agent — a variant of the o3 reasoning model fine-tuned for software engineering via reinforcement learning on real-world coding tasks. It is optimised to mirror human PR style, follow instructions precisely, and iterate until tests pass.

Anthropic's command-line coding assistant, which can read and edit files, run shell commands, and interact with a codebase. It supports a plugin system that allows third-party tools — including this Codex integration — to extend its capabilities.

The scaffolding layer that wraps an AI model to give it structured access to tools, file systems, and execution environments. A shared open-source harness means different front-ends (a plugin, a CLI, a web UI) can invoke the same agent with consistent behaviour.

repos.summary: An open-source Claude Code plugin authored by OpenAI that lets users invoke the Codex software-engineering agent from within Anthropic's Claude Code environment. It is built on the same app server and harness as the standalone Codex product, giving parity on parallel task execution and code-review workflows. The repository is maintained under the `openai` GitHub organisation.
